content: Working on ligand 1 again. Every productive link I have built puts the azine nitrogen immediately adjacent to the bridging NH - pyridin-2-ylamino and pyrimidin-2-ylamino both do - which means the NH and the ring N form a coplanar donor/acceptor pair, the classic kinase hinge arrangement. I have never tested moving that nitrogen away, and the answer changes how I design every future molecule: if adjacency is required, the 2-amino regiochemistry is non-negotiable, and if it is not, then any pyridine isomer will do and I have far more positions to decorate. Atom 6 is the aromatic carbon bearing the arylamine at atom 7, a non-ring bond, so I cut it and attach pyridin-3-ylamino instead - same atom count, same donor, same monocyclic azine, with the ring nitrogen moved from ortho to meta relative to the NH. Nothing else about the molecule changes.
